Those "ten dollar meal" things work out if you consider average bulk cost, etc, which isn't necessarily the way we all can or do buy food. Keeping a stocked pantry is critical for cooking at home, but it does add to the overall cost of things. There is a reason why processed, pre-packaged food seems cheaper to a lot of people, and that's because it is, unless you're very good at managing your pantry ingredients.

Fresh food will cost more regardless if you're buying prepared meals or making your own, but making your own is still cheaper.
